title: Functoriality of sheaf cohomology
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the abelian category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The global-sections functor $\Gamma(X,-):\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)\to\operatorname{Ab}$ is additive and left exact [lem-sc-global-sections-left-exact], and $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ has enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives]. Define $H^i(X,-)$ to be the $i$-th right derived functor of $\Gamma(X,-)$ via injective resolutions [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Then every morphism $u:\mathcal G'\to\mathcal G$ induces $H^i(u):H^i(X,\mathcal G')\to H^i(X,\mathcal G)$ and $H^i(\varphi\circ u)=H^i(\varphi)\circ H^i(u)$ for composable module morphisms.

source.place: Section Tag 01DZ (Cohomology of sheaves: cohomology as right derived functors of global sections)

proof.text: The module category has enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives], and the global-sections functor is additive and left exact by [lem-sc-global-sections-left-exact]. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor], applied to $v=\Gamma(X,-)$, says that the right derived functors $R^iv=H^i(X,-)$ form additive functors. Functoriality of a functor gives the induced map $H^i(u)$ and preserves composition, so $H^i(\varphi\circ u)=H^i(\varphi)\circ H^i(u)$.
